note: the 'ear tufts' are feathers, not ears; the wings fold flat against the body and the tail barely projects
Taller than wide when perched upright; the body is a rounded column, not a horizontal hawk shape.
normally drawn clinging vertically, so it reads much taller than wide; the head is often crested or red-capped
The unbroken sloping wedge from bill tip to crown is the key read; a normal duck's stepped forehead is wrong.
raccoon-sized, not bear-sized, and unrelated to the giant panda
Front legs are noticeably longer than the hind legs; the sloping topline is the defining read.
no shoulder hump - the highest point is the hindquarters, the opposite of a brown bear
the 'spectacle' markings vary and may extend down the chest; some individuals have almost none
